# MeedyaDL 1.13.0-alpha.47

_No user-facing changes since v1.13.0-alpha.46 — documentation and internal housekeeping updates only._

## What's changed since v1.10.2 (the last stable release)

### What's new

- The app has a new internal identifier (com.meedyasuite.meedyadl); this only affects how your data is stored on disk and does not change how you use the app.
- On first launch after updating, your existing settings, download queue, history, logs, and saved logins are automatically carried forward to the app's new storage location -- nothing is lost, and your old data is left untouched as a backup.
- MeedyaDL can now tidy itself into an /Applications/MeedyaSuite folder so all MeedyaSuite apps live together.
- Fixed a bug where a fresh install could get stuck with no way to finish setup if a newer MeedyaDL version was already out -- you're now offered a clear choice to update first or continue setting up on the version you have.
- The Spotify engine (votify) now has a validated, tested version range — installs and upgrades stay within it by default, and above-ceiling releases are clearly flagged as untested before you opt in.
- Spotify downloads now get an accurate, upfront warning when Spotify's servers are unreachable — even when the rest of the internet is working fine — instead of a slower, less helpful generic failure.
- MeedyaDL now explains when a feature or service has been temporarily paused, instead of it simply disappearing.
- If a download service ever has to be paused, MeedyaDL now explains why instead of failing silently, and anything already downloading finishes normally.
- On GAMDL 3.8 and newer, Dolby Atmos and AC3 now download without the Wrapper service (only Lossless still needs it), and the Settings text explains this for your installed version.
- Removed an obsolete "Fetch Extra Tags" setting that only applied to old GAMDL 2.x — MeedyaDL's own metadata already covers it with better accuracy.
- 32-bit Raspberry Pi setups now correctly recognise the last GAMDL version that works on their device.
- New "Test word-level lyrics connection" button in Settings checks your Apple Music lyrics access before a long download.
- Downloads that finish but produce unplayable files are now caught and reported instead of being marked complete.
- Clearer warnings when animated cover art can't be fetched because it's region-locked, plus a fallback so square motion covers still appear when only a portrait version exists.
- MeedyaDL now recognises tools you installed with more package managers (Homebrew, MacPorts, apt, dnf, pipx, Scoop, snap) and can update them through that package manager, instead of downloading a separate copy.
- If a system Python you reused is later removed or relocated — which a Homebrew upgrade can sometimes do — and that leaves MeedyaDL's Python setup unable to start, the setup wizard now explains what happened and offers a one-click rebuild, instead of just showing "Python not found". (MeedyaDL's own bundled Python is unaffected.)

### What's fixed

- Prerelease notes now always read in plain English — no more version-bump-only release notes. ([#1046](https://github.com/MWBMPartners/MeedyaDL/pull/1046))
- The download links on release pages are now tucked into a collapsible section, so the release notes are the first thing you see. ([#1046](https://github.com/MWBMPartners/MeedyaDL/pull/1046))
- The app icon now stays sharp and readable at small sizes, instead of turning blurry.
- Fixed a bug where MeedyaDL could fail to notice that a newer version of itself was available, so app update banners and prompts sometimes stayed silent.
- MeedyaDL now correctly spots newer test releases, so updates between preview versions arrive as they should.
- Fixed a rare issue where checking for a newer GAMDL version could hang for minutes on a slow or unreliable connection, delaying first-time setup.
- Fixed a rare macOS issue where the offer to tidy MeedyaDL into your Applications folder could interrupt an in-progress app update, forcing an extra restart.
- Fixed Spotify downloads and dependency installs silently failing on Windows for users who chose to reuse an existing system Python during setup.
- Spotify downloads now record accurate album information in their local download record, instead of misleading, Apple-Music-shaped data.
- Development builds are now fully tested before release.
- MeedyaDL now supports and recommends the newest Apple Music download engine release (GAMDL 3.8.5); 32-bit Raspberry Pi setups are unaffected and automatically stay on the last version that works for them.
- Fixed the in-app Help page showing the wrong "coming soon" version numbers for Spotify, YouTube, and BBC iPlayer support. ([#949](https://github.com/MWBMPartners/MeedyaDL/pull/949))
- Undo after Clear All or Abort now reliably re-queues every item, even for large batches.
- You can now paste Spotify links into the Download page (Spotify downloads still require developer access).
- Songs now correctly get their Apple Music audio-quality tags such as Lossless and Dolby Atmos.
- Lyrics and artist videos are now fetched in your configured language.
- New setting to choose animated cover-art quality — the new Standard (~1080p) default saves hundreds of MB per album.
- FFmpeg now installs from its official source on Linux again instead of always falling back to the backup mirror.
- Fixed MP4Box installation on Windows for user names that contain spaces.
- On Raspberry Pi, MeedyaDL now explains how to install GPAC in a terminal instead of failing silently when it cannot ask for your password.
- Tool downloads can now be checksum-verified, and the unverifiable GPAC nightly installer is no longer run.
- The setup wizard now automatically recognises FFmpeg, MP4Box, MediaInfo and other tools you already installed with Homebrew (or your system package manager) and reuses them in place, instead of showing them as missing.

### Notes

- The built-in help now explains what it means when a feature is shown as temporarily unavailable — it's deliberate, temporary, and nothing is wrong with your installation.
- Our documentation now explains the in-app notices you'll see if we ever pause a feature, and spells out exactly what the app shares when it checks for updates and feature availability — your app version, operating system and processor type, and never anything that identifies you or your library.
- When a service is temporarily paused, MeedyaDL now tells you why instead of failing silently, and anything already downloading finishes normally.
